lines.text: What bizarre physics happens if you try mixing boiling hot water with ice cold water in zero gravity?
On Earth, hot water naturally rises to the top because heat lowers density, driving convection currents.
In zero gravity aboard the space station, there is no up or down, meaning natural buoyancy completely disappears.
When astronauts inject hot and cold water into a single floating sphere, the temperatures do not circulate.
Instead of churning into warm water, heat can only transfer sluggishly through slow molecular diffusion.
You end up with a single floating liquid orb that is scalding hot on one side and freezing on the other.
In space, even simple liquids behave like strange alien substances.
